subject: Customer prompt retention, training opt-out, and DPIA evidence
messages:
From: Alicia Bennett <security@finserv-corp.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Tom Gallagher <procurement@finserv-corp.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 08:15:00 -0000
Subject: Customer data handling for LLMs — prompts, retention, and training opt-out

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team has a few follow-ups so we can close the DPIA and internal review:

- Do you retain customer prompts and model responses by default? If so, what is the retention period and where are those logs stored?
- Are customer prompts ever used to train or improve models (either Redwood-managed models or downstream open-source models)?
- What is the formal opt-out process for customers that do not want their prompts used for training? Is it self-service in the console or requires contract addenda?
- Can you provide a short evidence package for our DPIA that includes: retention policy excerpt, a sample audit/log extract (anonymized), and a statement on training usage?

We are aiming to complete our review by end of next week. If easier, we can hop on a quick call — Tom from procurement is happy to join.

Thanks,
Alicia Bennett
Security Lead — FinServ Corp
security@finserv-corp.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com>
To: Alicia Bennett <security@finserv-corp.com>
Cc: Tom Gallagher <procurement@finserv-corp.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood-inference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 12:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Customer data handling for LLMs — prompts, retention, and training opt-out

Alicia —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick answers up-front and I will follow with an evidence package and proposed wording from legal:

- Prompt/response storage: By default, customer prompts and generated responses are retained in our blob store for 30 days using customer-controlled encryption keys for hosted customers; customers on Private/Dedicated can set retention to 0 and disable storage.
- Training usage: We do not train Redwood production models on live customer prompts by default. Training or model improvement using customer data is only performed on datasets where the customer has explicitly opted in and signed a data-use addendum.
- Opt-out: Customers can opt-out via the Console toggle for hosted tenants (Account -> Data & Privacy -> Training Opt-Out) or via contract addendum for enterprise deals; for Private deployments data residency policies are enforced by customer config.

I'll loop in Neha and Monica from privacy and CS to package the DPIA excerpt, retention policy snippet, and an anonymized sample log extract. Can we schedule a 30-minute call Tuesday (Feb 23) 14:00 ET?

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0128

Attachments: none in this reply

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood-inference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood-inference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 09:08:00 -0000
Subject: RE: Customer data handling for LLMs — suggested DPIA wording and artifacts

Team —

Below is a concise package we can send to FinServ; Karthik please paste this into your reply and attach the files listed. I kept language conservative for the DPIA.

1) Short statement (for DPIA):
"Redwood Inference does not use customer-entered prompts or model outputs to train or improve production model weights unless the customer has provided explicit, documented consent through a contractual data-use addendum or has enabled Training Opt-In in the Console. For hosted customers, default prompt/response retention is 30 days; retention can be shortened to 0 days for customers who elect data-not-retained configurations. Logs are stored in encrypted buckets (AES-256) with access controls and audit logging enabled. Where applicable, data transfers are governed by the customer's chosen transfer mechanisms (SCCs for EU customers) and customer-managed keys are supported for Private deployments."

2) Opt-out mechanics (operational):
- Console toggle for hosted tenants (effective immediately)
- Enterprise: contractual addendum + account configuration changes implemented by Customer Success within 3 business days after signature
- Private/on-prem: customer controls retention via deployment config; Redwood provides guidance and scripts

3) Evidence/artifact list to attach:
- redwood_dpia_summary_20270221.pdf (one-page statement + contact)
- training-optout-policy-template.docx (ops steps to enforce opt-out)
- s3_prompt_logs_sample.csv (10-line anonymized extract showing timestamp, request-id, region)
- SOC2-report-ref-Redwood.pdf (reference pointing to our SOC 2 report portal; full report provided under NDA)

4) HIPAA/regulated note:
If the customer requires HIPAA assurances, the product supports Business Associate Agreement (BAA) execution for Dedicated/Private deployments only; hosted customers should engage sales for controls review.

5) Suggested timeline:
- Send artifacts and sample log today/tomorrow
- 30-minute call to walk through artifacts and Q&A (Karthik to book)

Let me know if any wording needs to be softened.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood-inference.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com>

Subject: Re: Customer data handling for LLMs — prompts, retention, and training opt-out

Alicia / Tom —

Per your request, attached is a short DPIA evidence bundle and an anonymized log extract. Key points:

- Retention: default 30 days for hosted customers; can be set to 0 via Console or by request for enterprise accounts.
- Training: customer data is not used to train production models without explicit opt-in / contractual consent.
- Opt-out: Console toggle (hosted) or contract addendum (enterprise); Private deployments controlled by customer config.

Attachments (zipped for delivery):
- redwood_dpia_summary_20270221.pdf (one-page statement)
- training-optout-policy-template.docx (ops steps)
- s3_prompt_logs_sample.csv (anonymized 10-row sample)

Call: I scheduled a 30-minute call for Tue, Feb 23 at 14:00 ET (invite sent). If that doesn't work, propose alternatives and we will adjust.

If you need our SOC 2 report or a BAA draft, let me know and we will route via our security portal / legal NDAs.

Thanks,
Karthik
